flags: Byway organization gives 72 miles and 2021 All-American Road status; material maps 64 miles and retains the older National Scenic Byway designation. The highway numbered A1A extends far beyond this corridor.

The byway homepage describes Gamble Rogers park as the terminus; its About Us page defines the southern boundary as the Flagler–Volusia county line. The story uses the park as the final narrative anchor without asserting it is the exact surveyed boundary.

Current unqualified oldest continuously inhabited city on the mainland is too broad. Cache 05 and archived FHWA 38 qualify European origin. Omitted the superlative rather than repeat cache 02’s broader wording.

No site-manager access page is cached for the lighthouse, Fort Matanzas or Gamble Rogers park. Retained their stories without opening hours, fees, ferry schedules or guaranteed entry. Fort remains a separate excursion; Wikipedia describes a boat crossing but does not establish current operation.

Marineland is retained as a municipality with a film-production origin, not a business recommendation. Cache 37 supports the 2020 population of 15, but that count is omitted because it does not develop the story.

Cache 36’s opening calls Fort Matanzas a 1740 fort; its detailed history separates construction begun in 1740 from completion in 1742. Followed the detailed chronology and identified coerced labor. No primary construction record is cached.

Cache 35 supports Spanish/British beacons from 1565 in its lead but discusses inconclusive archival evidence for the later coquina tower’s lighthouse use. Omitted an uninterrupted beacon chronology and focused on the documented 1874 replacement and submerged predecessor.

Driving order follows the material’s north-to-south strip miles. New Gamble Rogers coordinates come verbatim numerically from Wikipedia cache 34; all retained moment titles, coordinates and motifs are unchanged. Archived FHWA’s two-hour estimate is not a live traffic or access check.
